title: Good but unstable
body:
For simple spreadsheets this is great; it's useful because it's cross platform and has lots of features. For larger or complex spreadsheets it's frustrating as it regularly crashes. 

Sheets itself is stable (I use it online through Chrome or Brave) but the App isn't. I've tested this on multiple devices (iPads and iPhones), latest iOS and App versions. It usually saves the latest work, so could be worse, but it's very frustrating when your work flow is constantly disrupted. 

Edit 12th April '23: Large sheets - and some sheets with more complicated formulas - still crash the app. Also large sheets don't work with Offline mode.

Edit 21st Aug '23: App still crashing, I think this is sometimes with workbooks that have links to other workbooks, and possibly happens when background calculations complete (or timeout).

A recent bug that has recently been introduced: when copying a range with collapsed rows or columns, then pasting, the pasted range isn't consistent with the originally copied range.

I also have an issue with the auto selected keyboard. Often it selects the numeric keyboard, and pressing the change icon doesn't change the keyboard. I have to press the delete key when the cursor is at the far left position. This makes entering data cumbersome at times.

title: Really useful app… if it didn’t crash all the time
body:
I often need to update a spreadsheet on the go and being able to use Sheets is invaluable. 

However, the spreadsheet I use is very complex and the app simply cannot handle it. It crashes all the time (literally within seconds of loading up the sheet and starting to enter data) so I reload the spreadsheet and again it crashes within seconds.

It is very frustrating that a spreadsheet which was designed in, and therefore native to, Google Sheets, cannot be updated in the official Sheets app.

I only have good things to say about the app itself, which is very functional and does everything you need it to – as long as your spreadsheet isn’t too complicated!

Every time I enter new data into the spreadsheet, I have to fill out a new line of ten pieces of information (some of it from drop down menus and some of it by manually typing it in). It would be absolutely amazing if the app could recognise/learn this pattern (machine learning perhaps?) and then simply provide me with a single page within the app, so I can input all the data into a single page, away from the spreadsheet (as if filling out a form), before it transfers the info on the sheet itself, rather than by me having to update the spreadsheet by constantly clicking on individual cells and continuously scrolling what is a very large spreadsheet across a very small screen.

Hopefully improvements will be forthcoming for what could and should be an invaluable app!

title: Share spreadsheets with PC
body:
I installed Google sheets on my iPad mainly because I wanted the facility to share spreadsheets with my PC laptop. (At the same time I installed Google Drive on the PC.)

This has worked extremely well. If you move an Excel spreadsheet on the PC into a Google Drive folder, it's immediately accessible on the iPad, where you can view and edit it without losing its native Excel format.

Similarly, any Google spreadsheet created on the iPad in Google drive is shared with the PC, just as it would be on a Windows network.

Having used Excel extensively over many years, I have found the facilities provided by Google Sheets on the iPad somewhat limited  - the most irritating being that dates are in US format (ugh!).

Nevertheless, I would strongly recommend this app to any iPad user who needs to access spreadsheet files from both platforms.

I cannot emphasize enough just how bad this app is.

What I would advise Google to add to this app when they update this app is to add a variety of currency symbols, you can add currency symbols on the desktop version of Google Spreadsheets but you can't add any other currency symbols other than $ on the Google Spreadsheets app. 

Adding more currency symbols on the Google Spreadsheets app as well as the desktop version will be handy for people in other countries who build spreadsheets based on money and currency exchange rates.

You've just removed the entire folder structure that I have spent ages crafting, that makes sense to me in my life. Now, I have to look at one huge flat list and try to remember the contents of every document, so I can search for it, instead of simply going to my finance folder, or whatever, where I know the document has been filed.

I now have to bounce between the two applications. Use Sheets to write the spreadshhet, then use Drive to organise it. Rubbish!

Why on earth have you just broken google Drive, one of the best apps on any device?

Why not just introduce offline editing to Drive instead? I seem to remember it had offline viewing anyway, so why not just add offline editing as well as viewing????

If it ain't broke, don't fix it.

What an absolute mess.

Very angry, very disappointed.
